A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyTo work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing new content to be distinguished from relocated or renamed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DyTo benchmark results, video-length analyses, qualitative comparisons and measured inference times in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original DyTo benchmark results, including additional backbone evaluations and component ablations, alongside retained analyses and inference timings.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains temporally weighted hierarchical clustering, sampling within clusters and similarity-based bipartite token merging. The additional backbone evaluations and revised notation do not establish a distinct algorithmic change.

E1.justification: MVBench replaces STAR in the quantitative structured-VQA evaluation; the other four structured and five open-ended benchmarks remain. The Figure 8 laptop example is retained despite its attribution changing from STAR to MVBench, so that relabeling does not establish a new qualitative case.

E2.justification: Structured comparisons add methods including LLaVA-OneVision, LLaMA-VID and LLaVA-NeXT-Video, while removing Chat-UniVi-v1.5, DeepStack-L, LLoVi and VideoAgent. Open-ended comparisons drop FreeVA, MovieChat+, 34B PLLaVA and standalone LLaVA-NeXT-Image. IG-VLM and SlowFast-LLaVA remain, with the latter shortened to SlowFast.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from LLaVA-NeXT at 7B/34B to include InternVL2 at 8B/26B and Qwen-VL-Chat at 9B. New component-removal experiments introduce controls at 7B and 34B. Section 4.2 also revises the reported merge-ratio expression from r=L/K to r=Z/K, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 and Table 3 separately remove clustering and token merging across five benchmarks and two model sizes, directly testing component contributions that v1 did not ablate. Video-length analyses and the merging visualization remain, with the latter moved to Appendix C. Figure 5 removes one of three clustering examples.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or significance-testing procedures. Figure 3 already contains shaded bands in v1; v2 retains them without newly explaining their statistical meaning or estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial backbone, MVBench and ablation results. For retained 34B DyTo entries, IntentQA changes from 66.4 in v1 Table 3 to 67.5 in v2 Table 1, and MSRVTT-QA accuracy changes from 66.1 to 66.2. However, v2 Table 3 reports IntentQA as 67.3 and 7B VideoMME as 42.7 versus 41.2 in Table 1, without explaining different settings. Some baseline values also receive different benchmark assignments, such as SeViLA's 44.6 moving from STAR to VideoMME.

T1.justification: The temporal-distance, adjacency and multihead-similarity definitions remain unchanged. Cluster indexing and sampled-sequence dimensional notation are revised without introducing new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same training-free hierarchical/bipartite framework and claims concerning semantic preservation, efficiency and state-of-the-art video understanding. Additional experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: The new ablation discussion attributes clustering's limited benefit on NExTQA to short clips, interpreting the 34B result where removing clustering scores 73.2 versus 72.9 for full DyTo. Section 4.3 also broadens its comparative interpretation from outperforming several models to all fine-tuned models, although Table 1 includes a VideoMME baseline scoring 60.2 versus DyTo's best 59.3. Other mechanism and timing interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement, InternVL2/Qwen weight pointers and backbone/frame-length information in tables. Hardware and RoPE details move to Appendix B. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit 336×336 input resolution, token-grid dimensions, H=16 and initial merge setting r1=288; Appendix C's retained r=288 concerns visualization. Linked resources were not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LLaVA-OneVision, MVBench and InternVideo2 and removes the STAR reference. The related-work narrative and positioning against training-based and training-free approaches remain largely unchanged. Duplicate references and publication updates do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: Most introductory, related-work, method and concluding prose is retained. Changes include localized rewrites, notation clarification, revised analysis headings and relocation of implementation and merging-visualization explanations into appendices.

P2.justification: Four benchmark tables are consolidated into two substantially redesigned tables with backbone groups and frame-length columns, and a new ablation table is added. Figure 1 changes from one ten-benchmark radar plot to three backbone-specific plots. Figure 3 is enlarged and stacked vertically, clustering displays are enlarged, and the merging visualization moves to Appendix C.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and evaluations beyond LLaVA provide useful evidence about component contributions and applicability that v1 lacked. The reorganized comparisons and code pointer also improve usability. These gains are limited by omitted implementation settings, removed comparators and unexplained discrepancies between v2 Tables 1 and 3, particularly VideoMME 41.2 versus 42.7. The broader evidence supports a modest overall improvement, while reporting inconsistencies prevent a stronger assessment.
